prompt:
Transform the supplied tropical cove image into one finished, deliberate pixel-art scene. The supplied image is the sole authority for scenery, camera, framing, geometry, visible object counts, palette and lighting. Change the rendering medium only.

Preserve the 16:9 wide composition and original camera: extensive blue sky above; low wooded headland closing the bay across the left background; clear turquoise shallows filling the left and lower foreground; white beach sweeping from the lower right toward the central shoreline; dense shaded tropical vegetation at right. Keep their boundaries and relative frame positions closely aligned with the source. This is a sheltered cove, not an open-ocean horizon.

Retain the two dominant leaning palm forms with their distinct crown positions, long curved trunks entering from the right, and original overlaps. Keep the smaller visible palm at mid-right and the cropped/occluded foliage as shown; do not invent a total tree count or replace the overlapping crowns with a symmetrical row. Translate the long feathered fronds into readable stepped pixel silhouettes without turning the crowns into broadleaf trees.

Preserve the rounded pale pink/gray shoreline boulder group, its major stone placements and gaps, and the small separated offshore rock tips. Keep exactly one isolated reddish rounded beach boulder in the right foreground. Do not add rocks or turn the rounded boulders into sharp crystalline peaks. Carefully retain the crescent-shaped waterline, thin wash of shallow water, and scalloped wet/dry sand boundary; these are shoreline features, not a constructed path. No fixtures, buildings or text are present.

Keep bright daytime light from the upper left, clear cyan water, white sunlit sand and deep green/blue shade under the trees at right, including the beach-shadow direction. The bright upper-left/top region is diffuse glare partly clipped by the frame, not an outlined sun disk. Do not add a sun disk, sunset, golden-hour cast or new clouds.

prompt:
Add exactly one canonical Legacy female character from Image 2 to the existing central office chair in Image 1. Image 1 alone controls the environment, realistic rendered medium, camera, composition, furniture, props, existing text/marks and lighting. Image 2 alone controls the complete female character identity, proportions, outfit and illustrated rendering. Its multiple views depict one character, not a group.

Keep her recognizable narrow lioness muzzle, cream muzzle/chin, small black nose, amber eyes, arched brows, rounded ears and distinctive flowing layered golden hair as shown in the master. Preserve her athletic female build and master arm proportions. Retain the fitted plain black short-sleeve shirt with its simple shallow rounded neckline and black trousers. No polo collar, button placket, new buckle, accessories, added logos, male mane or male facial anatomy. Keep her face, hair, anatomy and clothing in the master's polished commercial mascot illustration with controlled contour work and sculpted shading. Do not make the character photographic or 3D.

Seat her naturally at normal adult scale inside the existing chair, centered between its side bolsters. Her hips rest on the cushion and her back is supported; she is not perched on the desk. Her head sits near or slightly above the chair-back top, with her face and upper torso clearly visible left of the monitor. Keep master-matched rounded hands and blunt natural nails. Let the desk, mug and other foreground objects naturally occlude portions of her hands and lower body; do not force both hands, feet or tail into view. Tail and legs may remain naturally hidden behind the desk. No grasping, moving or adding props.

Retain the original 16:9 frame and all unoccluded scene contents: chair, monitor/webcam, headset, mug, shield award, notebook/pen, closed laptop, dock, plants, shelves, books, globe, wall signs and window.
